key_terms.meaning: A plain JavaScript function that takes props and returns JSX; React renders it as part of the UI tree.
JavaScript XML, a syntax that lets you write HTML-like tags inside JavaScript; a build tool turns each tag into a call like React.createElement.
The moment React creates the real DOM nodes for a component and inserts them into the page for the first time.
Read-only values passed from a parent component to a child inside the JSX tag; the child can read them but never assign to them.
Data a component owns and updates itself with a setter such as setCount; an update schedules a fresh render of that component.
A named method such as componentDidMount or componentWillUnmount that React calls at mount, update or unmount; in function components useEffect does the same job.
A form field whose value comes from state and whose onChange handler writes back to that state, so state is the single source of truth.
React's own cross-browser wrapper around the native browser event, given to handlers as the argument e with fields like e.target.value.
A URL pattern such as /products/:id mapped to a component, matched by a router in the browser instead of by the server.
The placeholder a router fills with the component that matched the current URL; Angular uses <router-outlet>, React Router uses <Outlet/>.
A label after a colon that states the type a variable, parameter or return value must have, for example count: number.
The TypeScript decorator that turns a class plus its selector and template into an Angular component that Angular can render.
A directive that adds or removes whole blocks of DOM, written as *ngIf or *ngFor in the template.
A directive that changes the look or behaviour of an existing element, such as ngClass or ngStyle, without adding or removing it.
An Angular operator written with | that transforms a displayed value, for example {{ price | currency:'INR' }}.
A JavaScript file that runs in the background, outside the page, and intercepts network requests so a web app can work offline.
A JSON file, linked from the HTML, that gives the app its name, icons, start URL and display mode so a browser can install it.
A pure function (state, action) => newState that returns the next state without mutating the old one.
The single object that holds the whole application state in Redux and exposes getState, dispatch and subscribe.
An RxJS object that emits zero or more values over time and lets subscribers react to each value, error or completion.

takeaways: React builds a screen from small functions called components, and JSX is the shorthand used to describe each one.
Props flow down from parent to child and cannot be changed by the child; state belongs to the component that owns it and triggers a re-render when it changes.
A React form input is controlled when its value is bound to state, which keeps the display and the data in agreement.
A client-side router swaps components as the URL changes, so the browser never asks the server for a new HTML page.
TypeScript checks types at compile time and then erases them, leaving plain JavaScript in the browser.
Angular joins a TypeScript class to an HTML template with @Component, and bindings plus directives keep the two in step.
A service worker plus a manifest turns a normal website into an installable, offline-capable progressive web app, while server-side rendering delivers finished HTML for a fast first paint.
Redux makes every state change a plain action passed through a pure reducer, which gives one predictable, loggable store for the whole app.
Angular services marked @Injectable are created once by the injector and shared, and their HTTP calls return Observables that components subscribe to.
bank_note: Long answers are expected to show a working example with explanation: a component tree or binding for the framework questions, and a before-and-after flow for routing, state management and service-worker questions.

bank.q: Explain what a React component is and how JSX is converted into DOM elements. Use a small component that shows a name and a price as your example.
outline: Component = function returning JSX, name starts with a capital letter
JSX compiled by Babel to React.createElement(type, props, children)
React builds a virtual tree, compares it with the previous tree, and updates only the changed DOM nodes
Mount = first insertion of real DOM nodes; re-render = update of an existing tree
Example: Price tag component receiving name and amount as props

bank.q: Define props and state in React, and list three differences between them.
outline: Props are passed in from the parent; state is declared inside the component
Props are read-only; state is changed through its setter function
A props change re-renders the child; a state change re-renders the owner
Both are plain JavaScript values and both participate in rendering
State changes are batched and asynchronous; props are just the values received for this render

bank.q: What is a controlled component? Explain why React recommends it for forms, with a login form as the example.
outline: value={email} and onChange={e => setEmail(e.target.value)}
State becomes the single source of truth for the field
Validation can run on every keystroke and disable the submit button
No need to read the DOM later; the data is already in state
Mention the alternative, uncontrolled inputs using refs, and when they are acceptable

bank.q: Describe the four kinds of data binding in Angular with one template snippet each.
outline: Interpolation {{ value }} for one-way class to template
Property binding [src]="url" for one-way class to template element property
Event binding (click)="save()" for one-way template to class
Two-way binding [(ngModel)]="name" needing FormsModule
Also allow banana-in-a-box naming [( )] and mention that it is property plus event binding combined

bank.q: Explain what a progressive web app is and name the three files or pieces that make one.
outline: Manifest JSON: name, icons, start_url, display standalone
Service worker registered from the page, HTTPS required except on localhost
Service worker lifecycle events: install (precache), fetch (serve from cache or network), activate (clean old caches)
Installable on the home screen and usable offline
Contrast with a plain website and with a packaged native app

bank.q: Write a React component that keeps a list of expenses in state and adds a new expense from a form. Show the state declaration, the handler and the render code.
outline: useState([]) for the array and useState('') or a form object for the input
Handler builds a new array with spread or map, never mutates the old one
Unique key on each rendered list item
Controlled input with value and onChange
Correct camelCase event props and no direct DOM access

bank.q: Design the client-side routes for a shopping app with a home page, a product list, a product detail page and a not-found page, in either React Router or Angular Router.
outline: Route table with path and component pairs
Dynamic segment such as /product/:id and reading it with useParams or ActivatedRoute
Nested routes and an outlet to render the child
Catch-all or wildcard route for 404
Links use Link/navLink or routerLink so the page is not reloaded
Mention lazy loading for the product module as a bonus

bank.q: Write TypeScript declarations for a product object and a function that filters a product array by maximum price. Show one place where the compiler would raise an error.
outline: interface Product { id: number; name: string; price: number; inStock?: boolean }
Function signature filterByPrice(items: Product[], max: number): Product[]
Optional property marked with ?
Compiler error example: passing a string where a number is declared
Types are erased at compile time; no runtime check is added

bank.q: Build a small Redux flow: an action creator, an action, a reducer and a store, for a counter that increments and resets. Then explain how a component reads and dispatches.
outline: Action = plain object with a type and optional payload
Action creator returns that object
Reducer is pure, handles each type, returns a new object, default returns the old state
createStore or configureStore with the reducer; getState, dispatch, subscribe
React-Redux useSelector and useDispatch inside the component
No mutation of state; show the spread pattern

bank.q: Write an Angular service that fetches a list of cities over HTTP and a component that shows them, using the async pipe.
outline: @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) class CityService with HttpClient injected in the constructor
Method returns Observable<City[]> from http.get
Component subscribes or uses the async pipe with *ngFor
Handle loading and error states; unsubscribe or let the pipe handle it
Provide HttpClientModule in the module or provideHttpClient in standalone apps
Show the environment base URL instead of a hardcoded host

bank.q: Compare React and Angular as front-end frameworks. Cover component definition, templating, data flow, routing and typical project size.
outline: React is a library for the view layer; Angular is a full framework with router, forms, HTTP and DI built in
React uses JSX in JavaScript; Angular uses HTML templates plus TypeScript classes
React data flow is one-way by default; Angular offers two-way binding with ngModel
Both have client-side routers and lazy loading
Angular ships more structure and convention; React leaves choice of libraries open
Judgement: team size, TypeScript use, long-term maintenance

bank.q: A team's single-page React app has slow first load and poor search-engine visibility. Evaluate server-side rendering and a progressive web app as remedies, and state which problem each one actually solves.
outline: SSR sends finished HTML so the first screen paints before JavaScript loads; also helps crawlers
Hydration attaches React to the server HTML without rebuilding the DOM
PWA with manifest and service worker gives installability and offline use, and can speed repeat visits through caching
PWA does not fix first-paint or SEO; SSR does not give offline support
Cost: SSR needs a Node server and careful data fetching; PWA needs cache-version discipline
Recommendation should match the stated problem

bank.q: Explain prop drilling, then compare lifting state up, the Context API and Redux as ways to share state in a large React application.
outline: Prop drilling = passing props through intermediate components that do not use them
Lifting state up works for shallow trees and small scope
Context API avoids drilling for low-frequency values such as theme and logged-in user
Redux gives one store, pure reducers, devtools time travel, middleware for async
Trade-off: boilerplate and indirection versus predictability and traceability
Recommendation depends on update frequency and number of consumers

bank.q: Trace the life of an HTTP request in an Angular app from a button click in the template to the rendered list, naming every Angular feature involved.
outline: Event binding calls a method in the component class
Component calls an @Injectable service obtained through constructor injection
HttpClient returns a cold Observable; nothing happens until subscribe
RxJS operators such as map or catchError transform or handle errors
Template renders the result through *ngFor, the async pipe or a subscription with a stored value
Unsubscribe on destroy where a manual subscription is used

glossary.def: A syntax extension that lets HTML-like tags appear inside JavaScript, compiled into function calls before the code reaches the browser.
An in-memory tree of plain objects that React keeps and compares with the next tree to decide which real DOM nodes to change.
React's diffing process that compares two virtual trees and applies the minimum set of DOM updates.
The read-only object of values a parent passes into a child component.
Values a component owns, changes through a setter, and re-renders itself when they change.
A function such as useState or useEffect that gives a function component state or lifecycle behaviour.
A form field whose displayed value is driven by React state and updated through an onChange handler.
React's normalised wrapper around the browser event, passed to handlers as e.
A web app that loads one HTML document and swaps views in the browser as the URL changes.
A library that maps URL paths to components and updates the view without a full page request.
A superset of JavaScript that adds optional static types, checked at compile time and then removed.
The compiler working out a type from the assigned value, so an annotation is not always needed.
A TypeScript syntax starting with @ that attaches metadata to a class or member, used heavily by Angular.
An Angular class or template marker that changes the DOM, either structurally or by altering an existing element.
The link that keeps a component class and its template in sync in one or both directions.
A background script that intercepts network requests for a site and can answer them from a cache.
Rendering the first HTML of a page on the server so the browser can paint before any JavaScript runs.
Attaching client-side framework code to server-rendered HTML so it becomes interactive without being rebuilt.
The single object holding application state, with getState, dispatch and subscribe methods.
A plain object with a type field, and optional payload, that describes a state change in Redux.
A function whose output depends only on its inputs and which changes nothing outside itself.
A function that sits between dispatch and the reducer, used in Redux for logging, async calls or crash reporting.
A lazy stream object from RxJS that emits values over time to each subscriber.
A pattern where a framework creates a class's dependencies and supplies them, instead of the class creating them itself.
